research_question: Owned-page scope: Law Firm Marketing Statistics for Budget Planning. Planned sources and method: Clio Legal Trends Report and ABA marketing survey; compare firm-size cohorts. Build a source-labelled comparison covering law firm marketing budget and legal lead generation cost; record dates, definitions and sample limits. Sources are proposed, not verified findings.

research_brief.purpose: Give law firm leaders a source-traced set of marketing statistics for 2027 budget planning, separating channel adoption, paid-search cost, and intake responsiveness.
research_brief.audience: Managing partners, COOs, and marketing leads at U.S. law firms setting 2027 marketing budgets.
research_brief.data_period: 2024-2026 (Clio surveys 2024-2025; Clio intake study 2024; WordStream campaigns April 2025 to March 2026; ABA survey 2024); figures rechecked 2026-10-03 before sign-off
research_brief.scope_limitations: Secondary sources only. Clio channel shares are approximate because chart 4.14 has no data labels. Vendor-sponsored research (Clio, WordStream/LocaliQ) is labelled. No universal lead-to-client rate or revenue percentage is supplied.

content_gaps: No ranking page separates channel adoption, paid-search cost, and intake responsiveness as distinct measures.
No page compares 2024 and 2025 channel investment from the same survey.
No page converts legal cost per lead into a budget test without inventing a conversion rate.
Firm-size differences in lead sources are rarely shown with their source.
value_add: Source-traced statistics with year, sample, and method; a 2024-2025 channel comparison; current legal Google Ads costs against other industries; Clio intake responsiveness data; and a funnel-backward budget test that uses firm data instead of a generic conversion rate.
